rationale: The child has a narrow repository-local implementation boundary and all required source components are current, independently verifiable, and already completed. A one-shot orchestrator can call their public deterministic verification and generation contracts in a fixed order, pin exact inputs and outputs into an immutable loop-run record, and fail closed on source drift or private content without adding any scheduler, provider, Skill-application, adjacent-repository write, or external side-effect authority.
affected_boundaries: canonical governed loop-run schema and fingerprints
bounded local execution-record or dry-run linkage
outcome, regression, rollback, and proposal provenance
privacy and authority enforcement at integration boundaries
existing_assumptions: RTS remains the canonical repository-local structural ledger.
The completed child components remain independently verifiable packages.
The orchestrator consumes public package contracts instead of copying or rewriting child internals.
Current governed outcomes remain SIMULATED_ONLY and do not establish external success.
Human Review Ledger and Promotion Application Preview remain separate future children.

data_migration.notes: No migration is authorized. A future implementation may add append-only loop-run records and a schema, but it must not rewrite existing child records, outcomes, proposals, Assessments, Preflights, or adjacent repositories.

external_interfaces: repository-local filesystem reads for committed governed records
stdout for deterministic generate, verify, and summary commands
approval_changes: No approval, Skill mutation, application, adjacent-repository write, scheduling, provider, or external-action authority is granted by this Preflight.
A separate explicit human lifecycle revision is required before SELECTED or IN_PROGRESS.
Any future live provider, scheduler, adjacent-repository, real-run ingestion, or Skill-application capability requires a new Assessment, Preflight, and approval.
regression_tests: Identical committed inputs produce the same loop-run identifier, canonical content, and fingerprint.
Every required child verifier is invoked; a missing, failed, or stale child record is rejected.
All input and output fingerprints are recomputed, and repository paths cannot escape the repository root.
Raw prompts, credentials, customer data, provider payloads, private repository bodies, and forbidden private markers are rejected.
The CLI remains one-shot generate, verify, and summary only; no scheduler, network, provider, subprocess, shell, publication, deployment, send, or adjacent-repository write exists.
SIMULATED_ONLY evidence cannot be widened into external business or user success.
The learning proposal remains REVIEW_REQUIRED, NOT_APPROVED, and NOT_APPLIED.
Verification is read-only and detects governed source mutation before and after execution.
All existing FREEZER, component, unit, stale-index, and Unicode checks remain green.
hidden_dependencies: The implementation must inspect and pin each child package's current public verification entry point and summary fields.
Some children expose committed fixtures while others expose deterministic stdout records.
The execution controller may only contribute bounded local execution-record or dry-run semantics, never live provider dispatch.
The loop-run schema must distinguish source fingerprints from derived output fingerprints.
CI workflow path filters must include the new package, records, schemas, and focused tests.
rollback_boundary: The future implementation must be revertible by its merge commit and delete no existing child data. Loop-run records are append-only. No automatic rollback, Skill restoration, adjacent-repository mutation, or external action is authorized.
completion_conditions: A standard-library repository-local package exposes deterministic one-shot generate, verify, and summary commands.
A fail-closed canonical loop-run schema pins exact Asset Manifest, read-only evaluation, execution-record, outcome, regression, rollback, proposal, and pending-review fingerprints.
The fixed verification order requires every child verifier to succeed before a loop-run record is accepted.
At least one committed fixture loop-run is reproducible from exact governed inputs.
Loop-run records separately identify confirmed facts, assumptions, unverified claims, risks, authority state, and evidence references.
All authority flags remain non-authorizing; there is no schedule, live provider, approval, application, mutation, publication, messaging, or adjacent-repository write.
Focused tests cover determinism, source drift, privacy, path safety, missing verifiers, widened authority, and read-only behavior.
CI path filters and public implementation documentation include the new package and records.
RTS-FRZ-000008 is governed through append-only SELECTED, IN_PROGRESS, VERIFIED, and COMPLETED records only after separate human approval.
risks: An integration wrapper could skip or mock a child verifier while still emitting a plausible record.
The orchestrator could copy private or high-volume source content instead of retaining only approved summaries and fingerprints.
Execution-controller integration could accidentally expose live dispatch authority.
Component schema drift could make an old loop-run appear current.
COMPLETED could be misread as approval to apply a Skill even though proposal and application gates remain separate.
